comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Source read narrows the ask, and it is smaller than this card first stated.

herdr already does mode-aware encoding for clients - just not on the control stream. pane.send_input {pane_id, text, keys} encodes text with bracketed paste applied from input_state() (src/app/api_helpers.rs:25-35) and named keys with the same ghostty key encoder its TUI uses (:37-49). So the daemon is willing to encode for us; the JSON API simply has no way to say 'these bytes, for that pane, encoded as its modes require' on the channel we hold open.

That leaves three distinct gaps, worth asking for separately since they differ in size:

1. No way to read the modes. crate::pane::InputState (src/pane/terminal.rs:112-125) already carries alternate_screen, application_cursor, bracketed_paste, focus_reporting, mouse_protocol_mode, mouse_protocol_encoding, mouse_alternate_scroll, modify_other_keys, color_scheme_reporting - and already derives Serialize. Publishing it on the pane object is the smallest change that unblocks the most: local encoding stays on the open stream, so it costs no latency, and mouse becomes safe to send (a_27CTgqqdv).
2. pane.send_keys / pane.send_input cannot name the navigation cluster. home, end, pageup, pagedown, insert, delete and ctrl+alt+delete are refused with invalid_key (observed, corpus/herdr-0.8.0/input-path/). That is a parser gap in parse_key_combo, not a protocol one.
3. The API socket is one request per connection, so any per-keystroke JSON method pays a connect(). This is why 1 is preferred over 'add a structured key method': it keeps the hot path on the stream we already hold.

Also checked, and reported as absence rather than evidence: nothing in herdr's CHANGELOG (the Unreleased section is empty), its socket-api docs, or any TODO near the terminal-attach input path suggests planned work here. herdr terminal session control is not documented in the public docs at all. GitHub issues were not checked - that is where any public discussion would live.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
herdr's JSON API gives a client one input channel - terminal.input on a control stream - and it is a raw write to the pane's PTY (src/server/headless.rs:2852 -> apply_terminal_attach_input at :403 -> runtime.try_send_bytes). The re-encoding in raw_input.rs belongs to herdr's own App-mode client, not to this one. Captured: corpus/herdr-0.8.0/input-encoding/, findings in docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 5.

Consequence: Muster must encode for the pane's real modes, and no pane terminal mode is readable anywhere in the API. Application cursor keys, kitty flags, bracketed paste and mouse reporting are all guesses at the moment a key is pressed.

The ask has two shapes, and herdr already has the parts for both. Publish crate::pane::InputState (src/pane/terminal.rs:113 - already derives Serialize, already reachable as runtime.input_state()) plus the kitty flags from src/pane/kitty_keyboard.rs on the pane object; or take structured key events on the control stream the way terminal.scroll already takes scrolls and encode them server-side. terminal.scroll (apply_terminal_attach_scroll, :340) is the precedent: structured in, mode-aware encoding inside the daemon.

Sibling to a_26LAtaO6T - same argument, same guardrail: shared runtime facts belong in server state behind the JSON API.
title: Upstream: control-stream input is raw, and modes are invisible
